findings.problem: File I/O (fs::read_to_string) fused with parsing and domain construction; unwrap() on I/O turns a recoverable error into a panic
findings.failure_mode: Missing or unreadable path panics the caller instead of returning a typed error; the function leaks shell side effects into data loading
findings.fix: Extract fs::read_to_string to a shell-layer caller; parse_boundary function accepts already-loaded str; return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> with shell handling the I/O and mapping io::Error to a typed error

findings.problem: println! logging call fused into the parsing loop; side effect pollutes pure data processing with console I/O
findings.failure_mode: Every parsed record produces a console write; the function is not pure, not reusable in headless contexts, and the log output is unbounded and unconfigurable
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parse loop; move any observability to the shell layer via a dedicated logging callback or structured metrics, not ad-hoc println! in data processing

findings.problem: Unchecked index into parts[0] and parts[1] without bounds checking; split(',').collect() can produce fewer than 2 elements on malformed input, and parts.get() would be needed for safe access
findings.failure_mode: A line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields triggers an index-out-of-bounds panic at runtime instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Replace the parts vector and indexing with line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? to extract (_name, value_str) without index bounds checks; avoid split(',').collect() entirely

findings.problem: Lossy cast from u32 to u16 via as u16 silently truncates values outside u16 range (0-65535); parse returns u32 which can exceed u16::MAX
findings.failure_mode: A sensor value like 70000 parses successfully as u32, then truncates to 34464 as u16, corrupting data with no error indication to the caller
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::ValueOutOfRange)? or parse directly to u16 via value_str.trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) to guarantee no truncation

findings.problem: unwrap() on the parse result for value; any non-numeric or out-of-range field in parts[1] causes an unrecoverable panic
findings.failure_mode: A sensor line like 'temp,abc' panics with a parse error instead of returning a typed ParseError::Invalid that the caller can handle
findings.fix: Replace .unwrap() with .map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid)? and propagate typed errors through Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: Unbounded allocation: Vec::with_capacity via collect() with no try_reserve and no domain cap on the number of records; no max_lines bound checked before allocation
findings.failure_mode: A file with millions of lines exhausts heap memory; the function has no bounded allocation strategy and no try_reserve to fail gracefully
findings.fix: Validate a domain cap (max_records) first; replace collect() with Vec::new() followed by values.try_reserve(max_records).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation)? and push with len check: if values.len() >= max_records { return Err(ParseError::TooMany); }

findings.problem: No parse boundary: file I/O, parsing, logging, allocation, and Record construction are all fused into one function; raw primitives (str, Vec<String>) are never converted to trusted domain types
findings.failure_mode: The function cannot be unit-tested in isolation from the filesystem; callers cannot inject test data without mocking fs::read_to_string; the domain model is leaky and raw primitives cross into the core
findings.fix: Split into a pure parse_boundary function: pub fn parse_records(input: &str, max_records: usize) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> that takes a trusted string, and a shell caller that handles fs::read_to_string and maps errors

findings.problem: No typed error type; all failures surface through unwrap() panics instead of a structured error taxonomy (Empty, Invalid, TooMany, ValueOutOfRange, Allocation)
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish between missing files, malformed data, overflow, or allocation failures; error handling is impossible because every failure path is a panic
findings.fix: Define enum ParseError { Invalid, ValueOutOfRange, TooMany, Allocation } and use Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> throughout with map_err at every fallible operation

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists to measure load_sensors throughput or latency
no profiler evidence for allocation patterns or hot paths
no allocation audit showing try_reserve or bounded Vec growth
no command evidence that cargo clippy or cargo test was run
no second-ring evidence for any performance or correctness claim
residual_risk: The crate has 6 BLOCKER violations (hidden I/O x2, unchecked index, lossy cast, unwrap, unbounded allocation) and 2 MAJOR violations (no parse boundary, no typed error taxonomy). The entire function fuses shell I/O with core parsing and lacks any error handling, bounds, or measurable performance guarantees. No commands were run during review; static analysis only. Delivery is blocked until all BLOCKER findings are remediated.
